chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The length of the saddle-bag of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was one cubit, and when he prayed, he would place it in front of him to veil himself from those who would pass in front of him.

key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ: In front of him; the space directly ahead of the pray-er
key_terms.ذِرَاعاً: One cubit; a traditional unit of length
key_terms.رَحْل: Saddle-bag; a leather bag used for carrying items, here repurposed as a prayer screen
key_terms.يَسْتَتِرُ بِهِ: To veil or screen oneself with it

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet use as a prayer screen to block people passing in front of him?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific practice of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) using a saddle-bag (rahil) as a prayer screen (sutra), emphasizing its modest dimensions of one cubit. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes the permissibility and recommendation of using any suitable object to demarcate the prayer space and prevent distraction from passersby, reflecting the practical application of maintaining khushu' (focus) during Salah.
